title: A causal connector predicts a dependent downstream state
summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks a cause-to-consequence relation between adjacent record events, rather than merely listing two successive actions.

design.mechanism: The candidate scopes over a preceding condition/action and licenses a dependent downstream state or field.
design.unit: complete candidate occurrences with a bounded preceding event and following state field
design.contrast: candidate-bearing causal link versus matched sequential pair without the candidate, controlling record position
design.prediction: Following fields are more often state consequences conditional on the preceding event, with replication on held records; a simple sequence model predicts no dependency interaction.
design.falsifier: No held conditional consequence contrast, or the effect is explained by record position alone, falsifies the causal-link mechanism.
design.scope: cached admitted event fields; endpoint availability_unknown for independent causal annotation
design.related: Distinct from result latency, line adjacency, and transition-state proposals; retains sequential alternatives
